CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on the face

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is an 18-year-old female presenting with acne located on the face that started approximately two years ago and is present most every day. She denies associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. She reports acne is also present on the chest and back but not too bad. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing regularly, which she reports is somewhat helpful. Patient notes today is a good day for acne. Mother reports the biggest flare occurred when patient started school sports in the fall with associated sweating. Acne does not appear to flare with menses. Patient has been menstruating regularly for approximately two years.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies itching, bleeding, or pain associated with acne. No additional symptoms discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
None reported.

MEDICATIONS
Elf super clarity cleanser (evening use, sometimes morning use)
Toner (evening use)
Persa-Gel (evening use)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is in 7th grade. Lives with parents and sister. Household pets include a dog, bird, and bunnies. Participates in basketball, volleyball, and tap dance. Wears sunscreen SPF 30 in the summer. Morning skin care routine: wipes face with water and washcloth; uses Elf cleanser if face feels greasy. Evening routine: uses Elf super clarity cleanser, followed by toner and Persa-Gel.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Full exam performed except under underwear and bra. Benign nevi noted on trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules. Open and closed comedones. Erythematous papules on face, primarily on forehead with some on central cheeks and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Mild to moderate acne, mostly comedonal with small inflammatory component. Multiple benign moles on arms, legs, back, and abdomen with no worrisome features.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mild to moderate acne. Start topical therapy: morning routine to include mild cleanser and noncomedogenic moisturizer with SPF 30 or higher. Evening routine to include mild cleanser, followed by adapalene 0.1% cream applied in thin layer to affected areas a few nights per week, slowly working up to nightly use. Follow with Persa-Gel in thin layer and noncomedogenic moisturizer. Patient counseled that adapalene may cause sensitivity, dryness, or irritation, requiring sunscreen use when outdoors. Alternative over-the-counter gel options available if adapalene is expensive or not covered by insurance. Benign moles to be monitored. Follow-up appointment in six months to assess progress.
